decisions.reason: Do not retain the overstatement candidate under the conservative standard. WHO 2023 says usually diagnosed at least three months after illness, a minimum diagnostic threshold, and permits symptoms to begin after recovery; it says duration is unpredictable. WHO 2021 says usually three months, not an upper latency bound. Neither proves several-decade post-COVID latency, and current follow-up cannot observe several decades. But they do not establish the claimed upper bound needed to refute every future delayed effect. The full author sentence groups chronic hepatitis, post-COVID and occupational neoplasms as long-term biological disease examples supporting registers; a reasonable contextual interpretation does not necessarily assign the same latency to every member. Retain an unresolved overgeneralisation/temporal concern, not an admitted factual error. Long-term registry rationale survives independently. Root assessed the full proposition and preserves the supported components and relevant uncertainty.
